source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 195: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer: Variant 195 (Performance Analysis) — treat the hang as an unverified symptom and do not infer NCCL, network, or hardware facts. Use an authorized disposable allocation, least privilege, redacted telemetry, a finite watchdog, and no production mutation. Record launcher, framework/backend and versions, image, driver/CUDA, hosts and placement, world size, configured timeout, first blocked collective, test size, and synchronized timestamps. Build a per-rank ledger with expected and observed membership, global/local rank, PID, visible GPU and mapping, selected NIC/interface, rendezvous/store response, collective order, exit state, and sanitized errors. Verify equal rank sets and ordering, device visibility, store reachability, routes/MTU/firewall policy, container permissions, topology, GPU/NIC health, clock/configuration parity, and resource headroom. Falsifiable hypothesis: a named rank is absent or has an inconsistent/unreachable rendezvous or transport interface, so peers wait; falsify it only when all expected ranks join in the same order, independent authorized path checks pass, and repeated minimal all-reduces produce correct checksums. Run randomized matched single-node, reduced-world, and full-world trials with software, placement, input, and test size held constant; change one reversible factor at a time and enforce the watchdog. Measure per-rank join, first-progress, and completion latency in milliseconds, checksum correctness, timeout/hang, rank exit, transport diagnostics, and cleanup outcome, retaining denominators and negative results. Check confounders including stale store state, collective-order divergence, topology asymmetry, interface selection, device faults, resource pressure, clock skew, and container drift. Do not treat a longer timeout or forced interface as proof; stop, collect redacted evidence, restore settings, and rollback on repeated timeouts, corruption, unsafe resource pressure, or unexpected production impact.
